title: RuneScape Dragonwilds: Skill Progression Guide - What To Level & When
author: Primitive Nomad
description:
In this video I go over the general progression rules for character skills in Dragonwilds. As you progress through the regions in the game naturally you progress through power regions through materials. But Dragonwilds has a direct progression path that should be kept in mind while journeying through the regions of Ashenfall. I break all of this down to ensure your character is progressing at a steady pace along side the regions resources and gear sets.

everything that you're doing and grind cooking to 75 before getting into Dow Unreach, but I would say that Dow
Unreach is where cooking 75 becomes your long-term food target and investment. Doubt Unreach is also perfect for
setting up a really good farm. It rains a lot there, so you don't have to worry about watering, and you can build in the
central part of the courtyard, and you don't have to worry about enemy raids. This is where I actually have my main
farm and is the main place that I have my farm throughout early access. Now, at level 75, you're also completely going
to eliminate the chance of burning power level 5 ingredients. And power level six food becomes available, but that tier
doesn't become completely burnproof until 99. So, cooking has now transitioned from a skill that quickly
followed your regional progression into a skill where reaching the highest tier requires a much bigger investment. Rune
crafting has a similar change here. After level 50, law runes are the huge gameplay unlock, and the levels after
that mostly improve your rune economy and your rune crafting efficiency. At level 53, rune essent.
Level 64 improves elemental spirits, so they can identify concentrated endem events. Level 71 gives greater
siphoning, improving the number of runes you get from your essence. Then the higher levels start unlocking individual
efficiency upgrades for different rune types eventually including law efficiency at 94. So after rune crafting
50, the name of the game is really how efficiently can you produce huge amounts of runes without burning up your rune
essence supply. Now mining has the same shift. The skill itself isn't unlocking mythil ore for you. Your tool does that.
The later skill milestones are improving your gathering efficiency. Mining 36 reduces metal ore weight by 25%. Level
62 gives ore and stone storage, and level 71 reduces ingot weight by 50%. So, at this point, the skill progression
is allowing you to gather, transport, and process much larger amounts of material. Now, construction, artisan,
and farming all move in the same direction. Construction level 53 reduces the weight of construction materials.
And at 62, Eye of Oculus becomes even better by sending dismantled materials directly back to your character. Artisan
continues improving your production abilities with super heat getting stronger at 66. Overdrive eventually
upgrading at 80 and magical mending improving again at 90. Now, farming gives super compost at 60 and then rapid
growth at 74, which allows you to advance crops through growth stages. This is a huge quality of life and this
is going to be one of the biggest boosts in your efficiency for ingredients as well as XP for farming. Now, this is
very important because the next region is going to introduce many new elements to the game that you have never
experienced before in any other region. Now, these skills aren't teaching you how to use the basic systems anymore.
They're making systems you've been using for the entire game much faster and more
efficient. Fishing also starts reaching its later utility milestones. Fish NATO comes at 55. Its cooldown improves at
60. And then level 70 gives experienced angller an access to the angller's hat, which gives you a chance for catches not
to deplete the fish node. Now, if fishing is important to your food setup, 70 is one of the last really significant
milestones before you start talking about mastery for that level. 70 is pretty much where fishing caps out. And
at that point, you can continue to move on from there. And you don't necessarily need to grind the skill at all. Okay,
now we move into the final tier zone, Umbreal Sands. Yes, there is another tier after it, but it works completely
different because it is a raid itself. Umbreal Sands introduces power level 7. And again, this region itself is very
different than any other region in Dragon Wilds because it currently represents the top end of the normal
regional progression. Gathering is now in the late game tiers. You're using Myithil tools to gather ore and
different wood types. fishing moves into U rods and umbreal sands introduces higher level catches like monkfish,
desert soul, and beltfish. So once you're established in the desert region itself, your gathering setup is now in
the endgame stage. Farming also reaches its regional U tier. Now you're using U farming plots and growing things like
desert weeds, barrel cactus, pipe cactus, and bunny cactus. Now the late farming unlocks are about automation and
speed overall. Rapid growth comes at 74, mug explosion at 80, overgrowth aura at
90, and then the farming cape at mastery level 99. At this stage, farming isn't really about unlocking the ability to
cook basic foods anymore, about creating a highly efficient supply chain. Agility continues being one of the stronger
general progression skills again in Dragon Wilds. Their Umbreal Sands course, Lava Fields, unlocks at 65.
Level 67 gives desert borrower which gives you access to another fast travel network. At 70, you get reactive recall.
Then level 75 is huge because it gives you explorer adding an additional 75 maximum carry weight. Now when you
combine explorer with backpacker at level 50, agility has now given you a total of 150 additional carry weight.
That is a massive upgrade for dragon wilds overall. Now furthermore, level 80 gives razorbacked brower. Level 85 gives
Trailblazer, and eventually you reach the agility cap at 99. This is why I rate agility so high overall in all the
skills across Dragon Wilds. It starts by giving you double jump and air dash, which assists you in exploring and
getting around the map. Then it gives you access to burrows, which help you with fast traveling. Then backpacker
recall, and even more carry weight. Doesn't just make you move faster throughout the game. It changes how you
interact with the world throughout your entire playthrough. and it makes your game play that much more efficient. Now,
cooking is also worth clarifying in Umbreal Sands because there isn't power level 7 cooking tier. Even though the
region itself is power level 7, the current cooking progression tops out at power level six in Dow Unreach, which
unlocks at cooking 75, which we went over, and they don't become completely burnproof until cooking 99. So, you
don't need to be looking for some more cooking milestones and ingredients as you've reached this skills cap. And at
this point for cooking, everything is now about improving efficiency and eventually mastering the skill. Now,
overall, like I said, the next region is tier eight, eventually getting to tier nine with cauldra set. And this is the
raid. There are tier eight tools that you will use and gear sets, but to be honest with you, you don't actually need
to take on the raid with tier eight gear. Tier seven gear is going to carry you very well through the raid. Now,
this is why I think it's very useful to draw the line between progression levels and mastery levels. There are still
plenty of extremely good unlocks after you've reached the late game regions, like mining eventually does get things
like divine rock and further upgrades. Wood cutting gets the lumber backpack and more powerful actual projection
upgrades, as well as major wood weight reduction. Magic eventually gets vengeance. Rune crafting keeps improving
rune efficiency into the 90s. Artisan upgrades overdrive and magical mending. farming continues improving its
automation tools. And obviously, every skill eventually leads to its level 99 skill cap where you can get that
beautiful mastery skill cape. But I don't think you should look at all of these and assume you need them before
you're allowed to finish the regional progression, cuz you don't. Those are mastery goals. Those are great endgame
things to chase once you've completed the title. The actual progression targets are the levels that
fundamentally change how your character functions while you're moving throughout the game and progressing in your save
world. So overall, I know this video was very long. I think this is the best way to look at the skill system in Dragon
Wilds. Don't open the skill menu and think that you have 12 separate skills and you need to grind every single one
of them independently. A lot of them work together and will level up together as you're progressing through the game.
Just keep an eye on the region you're in. Look at your current power level of your gear set. Then look at the next few
skill milestones that will actually improve whatever you're doing. If you're early game, maybe that's double jump or
some mobility skill set or it's cooking or artisian or wood cutting or mining to boost those skills. Now again guys, you
can play dragon wilds at any pace and all of us are going to play completely differently. But I think it's very
interesting to take a look at the skills themselves and really see how they actually move through the progression
path for each region. And this is one of the biggest things that I didn't fully realize until 1.0 and I started a fresh
playthrough because I have been playing for so long over the past year since day one of early access getting tricklefed
all of these different updates and my skills were way above the level for the region that we were entering at the
time. So, I didn't necessarily fully look at what was occurring, but I always told my community that some of these
updates might not seem interesting to us right now, but when we start a fresh playthrough and new players who are
coming into the game on 1.0, these systems are going to be fleshed out in a very systematic way to work in unison
with character progression and power level progression through each region of the game. So, let me know what kind of
skills are you working on? What is your favorite skill? What is something that you really love doing in the game? Maybe
